name: Dumbbell Side-Lying External Rotation
summary: An isolation exercise performed lying on one's side to strengthen the infraspinatus and teres minor through resisted external rotation of the shoulder.

setup: Lie on your non-working side on a mat or flat bench, keeping your hips and knees slightly bent for stability.
Support your head with your bottom arm or a pillow so your neck remains in neutral alignment.
Grip a light dumbbell in your top hand and pin your upper arm firmly against the side of your ribcage, with the elbow bent to 90 degrees.
Begin with the dumbbell resting across your lower abdomen.
steps: Keeping your elbow pinned to your side and bent at 90 degrees, rotate your forearm upward toward the ceiling.
Lift the dumbbell until your forearm is roughly parallel to the floor or just past it, without letting your torso roll backward.
Pause briefly at the top to contract the posterior shoulder.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back across your abdomen under control.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you rotate the weight upward, and inhale as you lower it back to your stomach.
cues: Keep the elbow pinned to your ribs like a hinge.
Rotate from the shoulder socket, don't roll your body.
Move slowly and use very light weight.

common_faults.fault: Rolling the torso backward to use momentum and cheat range of motion.
common_faults.correction: Keep your chest and hips stacked perpendicular to the floor throughout the entire set.

common_faults.fault: Allowing the elbow to drift away from the side during rotation.
common_faults.correction: Keep your upper arm pressed against your flank; place a rolled towel under the elbow and hold it securely without letting it drop.

common_faults.fault: Extending or flexing the wrist during the lift.
common_faults.correction: Lock the wrist in a neutral position so only the shoulder rotates.

precautions: Use very light loads; the rotator cuff musculature responds best to strict technique and controlled tempos rather than heavy resistance.
